name: app_build_child
title: Build an App (portfolio child)
description: app_build minus parent-scoped phases — for portfolio children with fully-specified briefs.

phases.title: Prompt Contract
phases.purpose: Preserve the user's original prompt before any discussion, convert it into a clear execution contract, list hard requirements, non-goals, success metrics, production-readiness expectations, and decision rules for every later phase.

phases.title: Initial Discussion
phases.purpose: Establish a shared, precise understanding of what this app is, who it is for, the core problem it solves, hard scope boundaries, and measurable success criteria.

phases.title: Per App Product Brief
phases.purpose: Create a production-grade product brief for this specific app: target user, paid value, core loop, subscription value, competitive wedge, viral or niche growth mechanism, local-first behavior, cloud-ready extension path, and the real reason the app deserves to exist.

phases.title: Detailed Discussion
phases.purpose: Deeply analyze requirements, edge cases, constraints, assumptions, risks, and open questions, resolving ambiguity left from earlier phases.

phases.title: App Features
phases.purpose: Enumerate and prioritize the full feature set with an explicit scoring / MoSCoW model and clear in-scope vs out-of-scope lines.

phases.title: Design Discussion
phases.purpose: Decide UX flows, information architecture, key screens/states, and the design principles that govern them.

phases.title: Design Handoff
phases.purpose: Produce a complete design handoff: screen-by-screen specs, interaction states, motion notes, design tokens, accessibility expectations, and a professional Claude Design prompt or import plan if the run is configured to pause for external design.

phases.title: Ios Architecture Review
phases.purpose: Review the app as an iOS product before final tech specs: SwiftUI architecture, Apple framework choices, local persistence, privacy, permissions, offline behavior, StoreKit/subscription architecture, permissive dependency policy, and testability.

phases.title: Tech Specs
phases.purpose: Decide architecture, technology stack, data model, interfaces/APIs, and non-functional requirements with justified trade-offs.

phases.title: Project Plan
phases.purpose: Produce milestones, sequencing, estimates, dependencies, and a risk-managed delivery plan.

phases.title: Task Assignments
phases.purpose: Produce concrete workstreams, file ownership, forbidden edit zones, branch names, merge strategy, testing responsibilities, communication protocol, and a conflict-prevention plan.

phases.title: Implementation Readiness Gate
phases.purpose: Before any code is written, audit whether the product brief, design handoff, iOS architecture, tech specs, project plan, and task contracts are coherent enough for a one-shot production build. Resolve blockers or explicitly downgrade scope before build starts.

phases.title: Build Coordination
phases.purpose: Iterative build coordination via agent messages. Planning and task assignment only unless build_code_changes_enabled is true.

phases.title: Build Verification
phases.purpose: Compile and verify the generated app, then run bounded repair iterations against real compiler/test failures until it passes or records honest remaining blockers.

phases.title: Human Qa Checklist
phases.purpose: Create a manual simulator/device QA script for every important workflow, including onboarding, empty states, error states, persistence, accessibility, offline behavior, paywall/subscription behavior when relevant, and regression checks.

phases.title: App Store Readiness
phases.purpose: Prepare launch readiness: App Store positioning, screenshots/storyboard needs, privacy nutrition labels, permission copy, subscription/paywall review risks, support/contact requirements, and release blockers.

phases.title: Final Review
phases.purpose: Final review of completeness, consistency, risks, quality gates, and a clear go / no-go decision.

phases.title: Portfolio Audit
phases.purpose: For multi-app prompts, audit the portfolio shape: every requested app is a sibling folder, every selected app has the right workflow, child prompts preserve the parent requirements, and no category was silently collapsed. For single-app prompts, record that portfolio audit is not applicable.
